question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle z,6 x,4 y\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle u^{2},- v,- u\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
-1\le u\le 0,\qquad 1\le v\le 3.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u=\langle 1,0,2 u\rangle.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle 1,0,2 u\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=u^{2},\quad y=- v,\quad z=- u.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - u,6 u^{2},- 4 v\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- u)(1) \\ &=- u \\ T_{2}&=(6 u^{2})(0) \\ &=0 \\ T_{3}&=(- 4 v)(2 u) \\ &=- 8 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=- 8 u v- u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=- 4 u v^{2}- u v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{3}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=3}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=- 34 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=- 17 u^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{-1}^{0}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=-1}^{u=0} \\ &=17.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle 6 x,- 2 y^{2},-2\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle 3 u v,u,- v\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
-1\le u\le 1,\qquad 1\le v\le 2.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u=\langle 1,- 3 v,3 u\rangle.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle 1,- 3 v,3 u\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=3 u v,\quad y=u,\quad z=- v.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle 18 u v,- 2 u^{2},-2\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(18 u v)(1) \\ &=18 u v \\ T_{2}&=(- 2 u^{2})(- 3 v) \\ &=6 u^{2} v \\ T_{3}&=(-2)(3 u) \\ &=- 6 u\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=6 u^{2} v+18 u v \\ &\quad {}- 6 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=3 u^{2} v^{2}+9 u v^{2} \\ &\quad {}- 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{1}^{2}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=1}^{v=2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=9 u^{2}+21 u\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=3 u^{3}+\frac{21 u^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{-1}^{1}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=-1}^{u=1} \\ &=6.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the signed flux

$$
\Phi=\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S
$$

for the vector field

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\langle - y,- x z - 1,2 x\rangle.
$$

The parametric surface is

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\langle - v,3 u v,2 u^{2}\rangle.
$$

Use the parameter rectangle

$$
1\le u\le 2,\qquad 0\le v\le 2.
$$

Use the orientation induced by $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$. Enter an exact value.

*Hint:* The oriented area vector is

$$
\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\langle - 12 u^{2},- 4 u,3 v\rangle.
$$

$\Phi=$ {{flux}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametric flux formula with the specified orientation:

$$
\Phi=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv.
$$

Use the supplied oriented area vector $\mathbf N=\langle - 12 u^{2},- 4 u,3 v\rangle$.

Substitute the surface coordinates into the field:

$$
x=- v,\quad y=3 u v,\quad z=2 u^{2}.
$$

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\langle - 3 u v,2 u^{2} v - 1,- 2 v\rangle.
$$

Form the three signed dot-product contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{1}&=(- 3 u v)(- 12 u^{2}) \\ &=36 u^{3} v \\ T_{2}&=(2 u^{2} v - 1)(- 4 u) \\ &=- 8 u^{3} v+4 u \\ T_{3}&=(- 2 v)(3 v) \\ &=- 6 v^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Collect the polynomial terms, writing $g(u,v)=T_1+T_2+T_3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(u,v)&=28 u^{3} v+4 u \\ &\quad {}- 6 v^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive with respect to $v$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(u,v)&=14 u^{3} v^{2}+4 u v \\ &\quad {}- 2 v^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both inner endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=\int_{0}^{2}g(u,v)\,\mathrm dv \\ &=\left[P(u,v)\right]_{v=0}^{v=2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}H(u)&=56 u^{3}+8 u \\ &\quad {}-16\end{aligned}
$$

A primitive of $H(u)$ with respect to $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(u)&=14 u^{4}+4 u^{2} \\ &\quad {}- 16 u\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate both outer endpoints:

$$
\begin{aligned}\Phi&=\int_{1}^{2}H(u)\,\mathrm du \\ &=\left[Q(u)\right]_{u=1}^{u=2} \\ &=206.\end{aligned}
$$

The cross product includes the surface area scale; there is no extra normalization factor.
